title: Equal-scored results come out in arbitrary order: prefer tighter names, then newer files
problem: rerank (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1507-1536) gives the same bonus to every name that holds the words, whatever else the name contains: for `tax return`, 'Tax Return.pdf' and 'Tax Return - amended draft copy 2.pdf' both get 70 + 55 + 40. The +120 exact bonus (1516-1517) fires only when one word is the whole stem, so a multi-word query can never earn it, and there is no length or coverage term, only the depth penalty (1534-1535). The final order is `raw.sort_by_key(|h| Reverse(h.score))` with nothing else (584), so equal scores stay in arrival order: search location order, then whatever fff returned. For Any Kind, fff merges files and folders with `sort_unstable_by_key` on the score alone (fff-search-0.11.0/src/file_picker.rs:1335), which discards its own newest-first tie-break (score.rs:1032-1040). fff's modification score exists only for git-modified files (src/dbs/frecency.rs:420-430), so in a home folder nothing prefers newer files. Searching `screenshot`, `img` or `invoice` lists dozens of same-shaped, same-scored names in no meaningful order, where Finder and Spotlight show the newest first.
proposal: Two changes in engine.rs. (a) In rerank, add a coverage bonus after the loop: `bonus += 30 * matched.min(stem_len) / stem_len`, where `matched` is the summed character count of the words found in the name and `stem_len` is the stem's character count, so a name that is mostly the query beats a longer one, and a multi-word query that spells the whole stem gets the full 30. (b) Replace the sort at 584 with `raw.sort_by(|a, b| b.score.cmp(&a.score).then(b.modified.cmp(&a.modified)).then_with(|| a.path.cmp(&b.path)))`; RawHit already carries `modified` (1342). Mention it in the manual's Ranking and limits paragraph (docs/manual.md:360).
original_test_plan: Unit test on rerank: with words [tax, return], a RawHit for /a/Tax Return.pdf scores above /a/Tax Return amended draft.pdf at equal fff scores. Engine test with two roots so today's arrival order is deterministic: rootA/shot-a.png with mtime 3 days ago (std::fs::File::set_modified) and rootB/shot-b.png 1 day ago; a search for `shot` must list shot-b.png first (today rootA's hit comes first).
original_risks: The coverage bonus must stay below the gaps between rerank's tiers (40/55/70/120) so existing orderings hold; the reviewer checked one_letter_app_hits_dont_flood by hand with a 30-point cap and the order is unchanged, but rerank_prefers_name_matches and finds_apps_without_indexing_them need a run. Folder hits carry modified = 0 (1365-1373), so on an exact tie files sort ahead of folders.

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is real; half of the proposed fix is wrong.

Confirmed in code:
- `rerank` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1507-1536) has no length or coverage term. The +120 at 1516-1517 needs `stem == word || name == *word`, so a multi-word query cannot earn it. For `tax return`, "Tax Return.pdf" and "Tax Return - amended draft copy 2.pdf" both get 70 + 55 + 40 minus the same depth penalty.
- The final order is `raw.sort_by_key(|h| Reverse(h.score))` at engine.rs:584. It is a stable sort with no second key, so ties keep arrival order: root order (parts are joined in index order, 532-547), then fff's order.
- The UI always takes the mixed path: `files_only: false` (src/finder/mod.rs:1386) and the default kind is Any (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:320), which reaches `fuzzy_search_mixed` at engine.rs:711-713.
- fff merges files and folders with `merged.sort_unstable_by_key(|b| Reverse(b.1.total))` (fff-search-0.11.0/src/file_picker.rs:1335). That discards the `(total desc, modified desc)` order `sort_and_paginate` had just produced (score.rs:1029-1042).
- `get_modification_score` returns 0 unless the file is git-modified (dbs/frecency.rs:420-430), and neo_frizbee's `Scoring` has no haystack-length term (neo_frizbee-0.13.3/src/lib.rs:516-542).
- Nothing downstream re-sorts under Relevance (src/finder/mod.rs:1253; crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs:150,170).
- The manual (docs/manual.md:360) and CHANGELOG do not mention tie order, and no test in tests/*.rs or engine.rs pins the order of tied hits.

Where the claim overstates:
- For file-only searches (a Kind other than Any/Folder, or `files_only`, as `fff find --files` sends), fff's newest-first order survives the stable sort within one root. There the gap is only across roots, and between hits that tie only after rerank.

Where the proposal is wrong, part (a) `bonus += 30 * matched.min(stem_len) / stem_len`:
1. It divides by zero on every dotfile. `name.rsplit_once('.')` gives an empty stem for ".secret" or ".gitignore" (engine.rs:1512). Hidden hits are dropped only later, in `into_hit` (1399), so rerank sees them. The UI test fixture has `.secret` (tests/common/mod.rs:43).
2. It works against part (b) on the candidate's own examples. A length gradient splits numbered series by digit count: for `invoice`, "invoice-9.pdf" gets 23, "invoice-10.pdf" 21, "invoice-100.pdf" 19; "Screenshot (9).png" gets 21 and "Screenshot (10).png" 20. The oldest group comes first whatever the dates.
3. A 30-point cap is not below the tier gaps. The 40/55/70 tiers are 15 apart, so a mid-word match in a short name ("preport.pdf", 105) beats a word-boundary match in a long one ("annual financial report.pdf", 102). That contradicts the proposal's own risk note.
4. "Tax Return" would get 27, not the full 30, because the space is not counted.
verifier.implementation_notes:
All code changes are in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs and are cross-platform.

1. Tie-break (the core; ship this regardless).
- Add a free function next to `rerank`:
  `fn by_rank(a: &RawHit, b: &RawHit) -> Ordering { b.score.cmp(&a.score).then(b.modified.cmp(&a.modified)).then_with(|| a.path.cmp(&b.path)) }`
- Replace line 584 with `raw.sort_by(by_rank)`. Keep it before the dedupe at 585-586 so the higher-scored duplicate still wins.
- `RawHit.modified` is already whole seconds from fff (engine.rs:722 and 750; walk/zlob.rs:74-77), so no extra stat is needed.
- Folder and app hits carry `modified: 0` (1365-1373, 1468). They sort after files on an exact tie, and among themselves by path. Do not stat directories before the sort: that would be up to 20,000 stats per root.
- Change the hand-rolled sort in the test at 2247 to `hits.sort_by(by_rank)` so the test uses the real ordering.

2. Replace the coverage gradient with a step bonus, or drop part (a).
- After the loop in `rerank`, when `words.len() > 1 && in_name == words.len()`, add a whole-name bonus if the words spell the entire stem apart from separators:
  - every word satisfies `stem.contains(word)`, and
  - the count of alphanumeric chars in `stem` equals the sum over the words.
- Use `const WHOLE_NAME: i32 = 50`, the same margin a single-word exact match has over a prefix match (120 vs 70).
- This lifts "Tax Return.pdf" and "tax_return.pdf" above "Tax Return 2024.pdf". It has no division, so no dotfile panic, and no length gradient, so "invoice-9" and "invoice-10" still tie and the date decides.
- Do not ship `30 * matched / stem_len` as written.

3. Docs.
- docs/manual.md:360 (Ranking and limits): add a sentence that results ranking the same list the newest first, and that words spelling a whole name rank as an exact name.
- CHANGELOG.md, under [Unreleased] › Changed: one entry.

Pitfalls:
- `File::set_modified` in the test must run before `Engine::new`. fff reads mtime at scan time and the tests use `watch: false`. The existing pattern is at crates/fffinder-core/src/ops.rs:802.
- Hand check of existing tests with the step bonus: `one_letter_app_hits_dont_flood` keeps scores 148/110/95/80 (single word, no bonus). `rerank_prefers_name_matches` goes 226 → 276 vs 127. `finds_apps_without_indexing_them` uses single-word queries and is unchanged. I did not run cargo, per instructions.
verifier.test_plan:
All tests go in the existing `mod tests` of crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs (run with `cargo test -p fffinder-core`). They run on Linux and do not need the UI harness in tests/common/mod.rs.

1. Unit test for `by_rank`, built with `RawHit::file` / `RawHit::dir`:
- at equal score, the hit with the larger `modified` comes first;
- at equal score and `modified`, the smaller path comes first;
- a dir hit (`modified` 0) follows files of the same score;
- a higher score still beats a newer file.

2. Engine test `ties_list_the_newest_first`, modelled on `searches_a_folder` (2084):
- Create `dir/a/shot-a.png` and `dir/b/shot-b.png` under a temp dir.
- Before `Engine::new`, set shot-a's mtime to now minus 3 days and shot-b's to now minus 1 day with `File::options().write(true).open(p)?.set_modified(..)`.
- Use `EngineOptions { roots: vec![dir/a, dir/b], app_dirs: vec![], db_dir: None, watch: false, .. }` and `wait_ready`.
- Search with `SearchRequest { query: "shot".into(), ..Default::default() }` and assert the hit names are ["shot-b.png", "shot-a.png"].
- This fails today (root a's hit arrives first; both score the same at equal depth) and passes after the change. Two roots are needed: with one root and under 20 hits, fff's own order already puts the newest first.

3. Unit tests on `rerank`, next to `rerank_prefers_name_matches` (1866):
- with words [tax, return] and equal fff scores, "/a/Tax Return.pdf" scores above "/a/Tax Return amended draft.pdf";
- with words [invoice], "/a/invoice-9.pdf" and "/a/invoice-10.pdf" score the same;
- `rerank` on `RawHit::file("/a/.secret", ..)` with words [s] returns without panicking.

4. Change `one_letter_app_hits_dont_flood` (2233-2250) to sort with `by_rank`; the expected order ["s.txt", "Safari.app", "sketch.txt", "Notes.app"] is unchanged.

Existing suites to re-run, none of which pin tie order: tests/finder.rs (`searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing`, `type_into_the_search_field_and_down_arrow`), tests/server.rs (/v1/find), tests/columns.rs (`search_results_sort_by_folder`).
verifier.risks:
- The tie-break is low risk. It only reorders hits whose scores are equal, and it makes the order stable across re-runs, so rows stop shuffling when the index changes during a live search.
- Folders and apps have no mtime in `RawHit`, so on an exact tie with a file they come second. Such cross-kind ties are coincidental, because fff scores directories with a different formula.
- Newest-first is only guaranteed among the candidates fff returns. The mixed path truncates to `fetch` (at least 2,000 per root, engine.rs:665-669) after its unstable sort, so a tie group larger than that at the cut-off is trimmed arbitrarily. Fixing that would need a change in fff-search.
- The path tie-break is byte-wise per component, not natural order, so "IMG_10" sorts before "IMG_2" when their mtimes match to the second. This is cosmetic.
- The step bonus changes the `score` field that `fff find` and /v1/find expose (src/server/mod.rs:424). No test or doc pins those values.
- The step bonus can misfire on contrived duplicate words (`ab ab` on "abxy"). This is harmless.
- If the coverage gradient ships as originally written, expect a divide-by-zero panic on any dotfile hit, and numbered series ordered by digit count instead of date.

orchestrator_notes:
Two reviewers ('fuzzy-word-case', 'sorted-search-results'; both on the trunk, read their done records and commits, which changed Engine::search, rerank and the cut) measured a related fault that belongs with this brief. In the second one's words: Found, not fixed:
- The plain search lists different items from run to run when many matches tie. fff-search is asked for its best 2,000 per search location and cuts among equal scores in no fixed order. In the 77,559-file tree, consecutive runs of the same search share 265 to 396 of 500 items for `index` (every file under `index.crates.io-...` matches by its path), about 300 for `bench`, 325 to 377 for `readme` (a list of names only), and `makefile` came back with 342 hits and then 429. Refresh, typing the same words again, and the retries while indexing all reshuffle such a list. It was there before this change; what this change adds is that a sort click re-runs the search where a sort chooses (the chosen list is the same each time when the wide fetch holds every match). result-tie-break orders ties after the fetch and can't fix which candidates are fetched. Your tie-break makes the order of the items that are listed stable; it cannot choose among candidates fff-search never returned. See whether the list itself can be made the same from run to run at a cost that is small and bounded (for example asking for more candidates only when the last score kept ties with the first one dropped, or sorting what comes back by score and then path before the cut), measure it on a large tree as they did, and do it if it holds. If it cannot be done well, do the brief as planned and say what you found.
